headline: An OpenAI publicist cut in on Sam Altman's Vanity Fair interview and asked to move on after the editor raised a ChatGPT user's suicide, The Verge reports.
score_reason: Kept at 6: a documented exchange with OpenAI's own explanation included, but it concerns how an interview was handled, not a new safety finding.
importance_line: It bears on how openly OpenAI discusses a ChatGPT user's death, which matters first to users and families, then to the public and regulators judging chatbot safety, but it concerns one interview and OpenAI says time, not the subject, was the reason.
summary: The Verge reports that an OpenAI publicist interrupted Vanity Fair editor Mark Guiducci, saying she wanted to "move on", shortly after he asked chief executive Sam Altman whether he knew Laura Reiley, a journalist who wrote in The New York Times about her daughter's conversations with ChatGPT before the daughter's suicide. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told The Verge the interview was running over and the company asked for more time after Altman addressed the topic; Altman called such questions "some of the hardest questions" that anyone developing AI faces.
notes: Read in full. The Verge's own account of the Vanity Fair interview, with a statement from OpenAI. Same incident carried by several other outlets on 5 Oct (headlines only seen). Sensitive subject (suicide): stated plainly and without detail.
